provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Living and non living things
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify living and non-living things.
The pupils should be able to sort living and non-living things.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about things around us. Today we will learn which things are alive and which are not.

Content:
Living things grow, eat, move and have babies. Non-living things do not grow or eat. A dog is living. A stone is not living. A plant is living. A table is not living.

Class activity:
Pupils will sort pictures into living and non-living things.

Evaluation questions:
Name one living thing.
Name one non-living thing.
Does a car grow?

Summary:
Living things grow and eat. Non-living things do not grow or eat.

topics.title: Features of living things
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list features of living things.
The pupils should be able to explain how living things move.

Introduction:
We know living things are different from non-living things. Today we will learn what makes living things special.

Content:
Living things feed on food to grow. They move from place to place. They breathe air. A goat moves and eats grass. A fish swims in water and breathes through its gills.

Class activity:
Pupils will act out how different animals move.

Evaluation questions:
Do plants move?
How do we breathe?
What do living things eat?

Summary:
Living things feed, move and breathe to stay alive.

topics.title: The habitat of animals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify animal habitats.
The pupils should be able to name animals that live in water.

Introduction:
Animals need homes to live in. These homes are called habitats. Today we will learn where different animals live.

Content:
Some animals live in water. Fish live in rivers and ponds. Some animals live on land. Goats and cows live in the bush. Some animals live with humans. Dogs live in our houses.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw water and land habitats and place animals in the right habitat.

Evaluation questions:
Where do fish live?
Name an animal that lives on land.
Is the bush a habitat?

Summary:
Animals live in different places like water, land or with humans.

topics.title: Plant habitats
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify plant habitats.
The pupils should be able to name plants found near rivers.

Introduction:
Like animals, plants also have homes where they grow. Today we will learn about where plants live.

Content:
Some plants grow near rivers. They need lots of water. Mango trees grow in the bush. They need sun and soil. Some plants grow in our school compound. They need water and care.

Class activity:
Pupils will go outside and observe plants in the school compound.

Evaluation questions:
Where do mango trees grow?
Do plants need water?
Name a plant near a river.

Summary:
Plants grow in different places like near rivers, in the bush or in our compound.

topics.title: The sun and its energy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what the sun gives us.
The pupils should be able to explain why things get dry in the sun.

Introduction:
The sun is a big star in the sky. It gives us light and heat. Today we will learn about the sun and its energy.

Content:
The sun gives us light to see during the day. It gives us heat to keep us warm. When we put clothes in the sun, they get dry because the sun takes away the water. During harmattan, the sun feels very hot.

Class activity:
Pupils will wet a piece of cloth and hang it in the sun to observe how it gets dry.

Evaluation questions:
What does the sun give us?
Why do clothes get dry in the sun?
Is the sun hot or cold?

Summary:
The sun gives us light and heat. It makes wet things dry.

topics.title: Forms of energy: light
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify sources of light.
The pupils should be able to explain why we need light.

Introduction:
We use light every day. Light is a form of energy. Today we will learn about light and its sources.

Content:
Light helps us see things. The sun is a source of light. A torch is a source of light. A candle is a source of light. When there is no light, we cannot see well at night.

Class activity:
Pupils will list things that give light in their homes.

Evaluation questions:
What helps us see in the dark?
Is the moon a source of light?
Name two sources of light.

Summary:
Light helps us see. The sun, torch and candle are sources of light.

topics.title: Forms of energy: heat
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify hot and cold objects.
The pupils should be able to explain why we handle hot objects with care.

Introduction:
Some things feel hot and some feel cold. Heat is a form of energy. Today we will learn about heat.

Content:
Hot objects have more heat energy. Cold objects have less heat energy. A pot of soup is hot. We use a cloth to hold it. Water from the fridge is cold. We handle hot things carefully not to burn our hands.

Class activity:
Pupils will touch objects with teacher guidance and say if they are hot or cold.

Evaluation questions:
Is ice hot or cold?
Why do we use a cloth to hold hot pots?
What makes things hot?

Summary:
Hot objects have more heat. We handle hot things with care.

topics.title: Simple machines
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify simple machines.
The pupils should be able to explain how a lever makes work easy.

Introduction:
We use tools to make work easier. These tools are simple machines. Today we will learn about simple machines.

Content:
A lever is a simple machine. A seesaw is a lever. A spoon is a lever. They help us lift heavy things with less effort. When we use a spoon to scoop beans, we use less energy.

Class activity:
Pupils will use a spoon to scoop rice from a bowl to see how it makes work easy.

Evaluation questions:
Name a simple machine.
How does a lever help us?
Is a knife a simple machine?

Summary:
Simple machines like levers make work easier for us.

topics.title: Moving things: push and pull
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate push and pull actions.
The pupils should be able to give examples of push and pull in daily life.

Introduction:
We use force to move things. Force can be a push or a pull. Today we will learn about push and pull.

Content:
When we push something, we move it away from us. When we pull something, we move it towards us. We push a door to open it. We pull a rope to ring the bell. We push a danfo to move it.

Class activity:
Pupils will push and pull objects in the classroom and name the action.

Evaluation questions:
What happens when you push a box?
Do we push or pull a rope?
Give another example of push.

Summary:
Push moves things away. Pull moves things towards us.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer questions on term's work.
The pupils should be able to participate in class quiz.

Introduction:
Today we will revise all we learned this term. We will have a fun quiz to see what we remember.

Content:
We will review living and non-living things, animal habitats, plant habitats, sun energy, light, heat, simple machines and push-pull. We will answer questions on these topics.

Class activity:
Pupils will be divided into teams for a quiz competition.

Evaluation questions:
Name two living things.
Where do fish live?
What does the sun give us?
Is a spoon a simple machine?
What is push?

Summary:
We revised all we learned this term and had fun with the quiz.
